- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction.
- If model shows gradual upward trend with low sentiment (≤0.33), true price often reverses or dips; expect mean reversion or sudden drop.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > history peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope after spike.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00), model tends to lag behind true price; adjust forecast to align with recent sentiment shifts.
- In low-sentiment environments (sentiment ≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to account for hidden demand or policy effects.
- For 30-day horizon, if true price deviates >10% from forecast in first 5 days, adjust model to reflect sentiment-driven volatility early.
- When sentiment is high and price is falling, model often ignores sentiment; if sentiment >0.67 and price drops, reduce forecast slope to match sentiment.
- If model forecast is flat or slowly rising while sentiment is rising, true price often spikes later; anticipate and adjust upward early if sentiment >0.67.
